wholeCandidateGoal.title: Alternatives Spleißen für Proteinvielfalt erklären
wholeCandidateGoal.titleEn: Explain Alternative Splicing for Protein Diversity
wholeCandidateGoal.description: Die lernende Person kann den Beitrag alternativen Spleißens zur Proteinvielfalt bei Eukaryoten erklären und die Bedeutung dieser Vielfalt für Selektionsprozesse in der Evolution einordnen, wenn relevante Unterschiede erblich sind und den Fortpflanzungserfolg beeinflussen.
wholeCandidateGoal.descriptionEn: The learner can explain the contribution of alternative splicing to protein diversity in eukaryotes and contextualize the significance of this diversity for evolutionary selection processes when relevant differences are heritable and affect reproductive success.

resourceLinks.title: Visualisierung: Alternatives Spleißen für Proteinvielfalt erklären
resourceLinks.description: Ein schematisches Gen liefert eine prä-mRNA mit vier Exonblöcken. Alternatives Spleißen erzeugt hier E1–E2–E4 oder E1–E3–E4 und damit zwei mögliche Proteinvarianten. Voraussetzung sind passende Leseraster und weitere funktionelle Bedingungen; nicht jedes Gen benötigt alternatives Spleißen.
resourceLinks.altText: Aus einer prä-mRNA mit E1, E2, E3 und E4 entstehen zwei reife mRNAs: E1–E2–E4 und E1–E3–E4. Darunter liegen unterschiedliche abstrakte Proteinvarianten mit gemeinsamem Anfang und Ende.

kindReason: This is an assessable biological explanation and conditional evolutionary interpretation of one mechanism. It is neither motivation, a recall deck, an exam/practice endpoint nor structural navigation. Stable prerequisite and LK/SekII roles are retained. The technical fingerprint alone was not treated as the decision.
atomicityReason: Alternative exon selection, resulting functional isoforms and the conditional evolutionary role of that variation form one connected mechanism-to-consequence explanation. The second clause interprets the same variation, rather than introducing an unrelated independently taught routine. Both finite cases require the same causal chain; the inherited-regulation case distinguishes it from somatic plasticity and equal fitness. No scope broadening or goal split is needed.
memoryReason: Evidence is constructing and evaluating exon routes, functional-frame limits and heritability/fitness conditions in changed models. The supplied exon letters and fictional R/r values are task data, not necessary recall items. Reciting splice terminology or fitness definitions cannot demonstrate this goal. No goal-specific memory deck or card is justified by the semantic clarification. This does not assert a new review of the whole existing card/visibility layer.
sourceInterpretation: The actual BY12 EA clause connects protein diversity to selection. The candidate preserves that connection while explicitly naming biological conditions; it does not declare alternative splicing universally necessary for selection. Original source decision, edge, passage, whole44 partners and source approval limits remain unchanged.
